scenarios.draft: Test listing and searching board feature assignments across multiple boards with assorted filters: by feature_key, by board id, pagination (page/size), and creation date ranges. Validate results change according to the applied search input and pagination settings. Confirm that only authorized roles (typically admins or advanced moderators) may retrieve non-public or system-level features. Test with invalid combinations (e.g., non-existent feature_key or board id) to ensure appropriate empty results or validation errors are returned.

dependencies.purpose: Create multiple discussion boards to assign different features to and support board-based filtering in test scenarios.
Create at least two different board feature assignments for applying filters and list coverage in subsequent queries.

scenarios.draft: Validate retrieval of a specific board feature assignment using its unique ID. Verify that for a legitimate, existing record and authorized user, all fields are returned correctly. Confirm that attempting to access a soft-deleted or non-existent board feature id returns the appropriate error (404). Test boundary with users lacking sufficient permissions to assert that access is denied as specified by RBAC.

dependencies.purpose: Create a discussion board for associating a feature assignment.
Create a board feature assignment; capture its resulting id for the detail fetch test.

scenarios.draft: Test successful creation of a board feature assignment using a valid feature_key and board_id. Validate that the assignment is stored and auditable. Upon creation, retrieve and confirm the record persists with correct values and metadata. Attempt to assign the same feature_key twice to the same board and verify a conflict or uniqueness violation error (409). Include both successful and duplicate/failure scenarios. Also, test for proper authorization enforcement (reject unauthorized attempts).

dependencies.purpose: Create a board to assign features to. Required for referencing board_id during feature assignment.

scenarios.draft: Verify that an authorized user (admin or advanced moderator) can update permitted fields of a board feature assignment (such as feature_key, enabled state, or description). Validate changes are reflected in the updated record and that audit logging is triggered. If attempting to update the (board_id, feature_key) pair to a combination that already exists, the test should expect a uniqueness constraint error. Also, attempt to update with non-existent id or with insufficient privileges, verifying correct error responses.

dependencies.purpose: Create two boards for creating and reassigning features between them.
Create initial feature assignments on different boards for testing update, reassign, and uniqueness conflicts.

scenarios.draft: Test successful soft deletion of a board feature assignment by authorized user (admin or advanced moderator): verify the record is no longer queryable. After deletion, attempts to retrieve the assignment should result in not found (404) or logical equivalent. Attempt deletion with insufficient privileges to ensure enforcement of RBAC. Try deleting with a non-existent ID to confirm correct error response, and check that audit logging for deletion is performed as expected.

dependencies.purpose: Create a board for assigning a feature flag.
Create a board feature to enable subsequent delete operations and validation.

scenarios.draft: Verify that an admin can retrieve a paginated and filtered list of system configurations. Create multiple configuration records (with varying keys, value_types, and descriptions) and perform a PATCH request with pagination, filter by key, and sort order. Ensure only configuration records that match the filter criteria are returned, and page metadata is correct. Validate role limitations—non-admin users should receive a permissions error if attempting access.

dependencies.purpose: Create diverse configuration records to be retrieved and validated during list and filter operations.

scenarios.draft: Test that an admin can retrieve the details of an existing configuration entry using a valid UUID. Ensure all fields (config_key, config_value, value_type, description, timestamps) are returned as expected. Then, attempt to retrieve using an invalid or non-existent UUID and verify a 404 error is returned. Also, attempt access with a non-admin role and expect a 403 permission error.

dependencies.purpose: Create a configuration entry used for successful retrieval and for generating a valid UUID.

scenarios.draft: Verify that an admin can create a new configuration record by supplying valid config_key, config_value, value_type, and description. Check that the system enforces uniqueness for config_key—by first creating a configuration and then attempting to create another with the same key, expecting a 409 conflict or validation error. Also, test failure modes for missing required properties or invalid value_type.

Verify that an admin can update editable fields—config_value, value_type, description—of an existing configuration via PUT. Attempt to update immutable fields (id or config_key) and confirm that such changes are disallowed with validation errors. Test correct auditing by updating configuration values and ensuring updated_at is changed. Also, attempt to update a non-existent configuration and expect a 404 error.

dependencies.purpose: Create a configuration record to be updated in the test scenario.

scenarios.draft: Test that an admin can perform a soft-delete on a configuration using a valid UUID and that subsequent deletes are idempotent (return success even if already deleted). After deletion, ensure the configuration no longer appears in active listings but remains in the record set for compliance. Attempt to delete a non-existent ID and verify that a 404 error is returned. Confirm all actions are audit-logged.

dependencies.purpose: Create a configuration record to be deleted in the test scenario.

scenarios.draft: Test listing of post dislikes with advanced filtering parameters: by member ID, post ID, and date range. Create multiple posts from different members and add post dislikes under different circumstances. Try searching with each combination of filters and pagination. Confirm the system only returns dislike records matching the filters and appropriately paginates the result set. Attempt to apply invalid filters to validate error response.

dependencies.purpose: Create multiple member accounts to be able to author and dislike posts.
Create several posts by different members that will be targets for dislikes.
Add post dislikes from various members to different posts to set up records for filtering.

scenarios.draft: Test getting a single post dislike record by ID. First, create a member, a post, and a post dislike entry. Retrieve the dislike by its ID as the owner, as a moderator/admin, and as an unrelated member to check proper access control. Also attempt to fetch a non-existent dislike ID to verify not-found error handling.

dependencies.purpose: Create members for acting as disliking user, admin/moderator, and unrelated user.
Create a post to be disliked.
Create a post dislike for the post by the member.

scenarios.draft: Test creating a new post dislike as an authenticated member. Create a post as one user, log in as another, and successfully dislike the post. Validate that only one dislike per post per user is possible, and that a duplicate attempt returns the expected 409 conflict error.

dependencies.purpose: Create two members, one as post author and the other as the disliking member.
Create a post to be disliked.

scenarios.draft: Test error handling when trying to dislike a non-existent post or when unauthenticated. Attempt to create a dislike for an invalid post_id (random UUID) and as a not-logged-in user, confirming that appropriate validation and authentication errors are returned.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member for authentication context.

scenarios.draft: Test updating metadata fields of a post dislike record as an admin or moderator. Create a member, post, dislike, then perform an update (such as changing the audit timestamp or metadata) as an admin. Confirm only admins/moderators can update and that attempts by regular members are denied. Also check business rules around which fields are mutable.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member as the disliking user and another as the admin/moderator.
Create a post to be disliked.
Create a dislike to be updated.

scenarios.draft: Test deleting a post dislike record. Create a post dislike, then attempt to delete it as the member who created it and as an admin/moderator. Confirm the like is no longer returned from search/list endpoints. Attempt to delete a non-existent dislike and expect an idempotent or not-found result. Try deletion as an unrelated member to verify permission enforcement.

dependencies.purpose: Create members for owner, unrelated user, and admin/moderator roles.
Create a post to be disliked.
Create a dislike that will be the target of deletion.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieval of member history logs with varied filters. Prepare several member history records with distinctive event types, member relations, timestamps, and actors. As an admin, issue a list operation with filters by member, event type, and recent date range to validate correct pagination and filtering. Repeat as a moderator role. Confirm audit logs and restricted roles (non-admin/moderator) cannot access all histories. Validate proper summary structure in response and server rejection of malformed query criteria.

dependencies.purpose: Create member records to link with member history entries and to serve as actors/targets in test records. This ensures realistic references for filtering.
Insert multiple member history events tied to the created members with varied event types and timestamps for a diverse dataset for searching.

scenarios.draft: Test successful and failed retrieval of a single member history event by UUID. Create a member history record and fetch it by returned ID, expecting full event details. Attempt retrieval with a random non-existent or previously deleted UUID to confirm 404 error. Also check unauthorized roles receive 403 as appropriate.

dependencies.purpose: Create members to reference in the member history, ensuring data refers to valid member IDs.
Create member history event for a known ID retrieval test.

scenarios.draft: Test creation of a member history event log as admin/moderator. Prepare a valid member, then post a history record with valid change_type, details, and all foreign keys. Validate that audit log is written and all event data is returned. Attempt creation with missing required fields, invalid member reference, or forbidden (non-admin/moderator) user, asserting correct validation or forbidden errors are returned.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member whose actions or changes will be tracked in the history for valid referencing.

scenarios.draft: Test updating a member history event as an authorized admin. First create a record, then update a mutable field (e.g., details or event type), confirming changes are persisted. Attempt to update a non-existent record (should return 404), and attempt updates with invalid fields or by unauthorized user (should fail). Validate that changes are reflected in the audit trail.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member to establish valid history event relationships.
Create an initial member history event for update test.

scenarios.draft: Test soft-deletion of a member history entry by its ID as admin. Create an event, then delete it, verifying deleted_at is set (soft-delete) and record is not returned in default list queries. Try deleting with insufficient permission (non-admin), and deleting a non-existent or already-deleted record, expecting correct error. Ensure deletion does not break audit trails or data integrity for related member.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member for the member history event link.
Insert a member history record for deletion scenario.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieving a paginated, filtered list of post report entries under various scenarios. Cover at least: 1) An admin or moderator successfully retrieves all reports with advanced filters (e.g., filter by reporter, post ID, status, time, etc.) and correct pagination metadata is included; 2) A regular member attempts to retrieve reports and only sees their own, never other members'; 3) Error scenarios such as requesting with invalid filters, out-of-range paging, or missing required filter properties; 4) Permission errors for unauthorized users attempting to access this endpoint. Validate result set matches role-based access and filter criteria.

dependencies.purpose: Register one or more members to act as report authors and post creators.
Create posts that can later be reported. Needed to generate valid post IDs for reports.
File several post reports with varying combinations of reporter, post, and reason to set up test data for listing and filtering.
Create an admin account for privileged access to post reports.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieving a specific post report by its unique ID via GET /discussionboard/postReports/{id}. Cover these paths: 1) The report's author (member) retrieves their own report successfully; 2) An authorized moderator or admin retrieves any report; 3) A member attempts to get a report they do not own and receives a proper permission/forbidden error; 4) Attempt to retrieve a non-existent or already-deleted report, verifying the system returns the correct not found error; 5) Invalid or malformed ID format is provided, resulting in a validation error. Ensure responses contain correct details or error structures according to RBAC and input validity.

dependencies.purpose: Register member(s) who will submit post reports.
Create posts to be reported. Required to have valid post IDs for report creation.
Create a post report to get a valid report ID for retrieval.
Create admin (and if applicable, moderator) user to test role-based access.

scenarios.draft: Test filing a report against a post via POST /discussionboard/postReports. Cover successful report creation with valid member, post, and reason codes. Attempt to submit a report for a non-existent post and expect a not found error. Try to file the same report (same member and post within anti-spam window) twice and verify a 409 conflict or validation error is returned. Attempt to self-report as the author and confirm failure due to business rule. Check permission error for unauthenticated user. Validate the audit log entry occurs after creation (if possible).

dependencies.purpose: Create member(s) for valid and duplicate report use cases.
Generate posts that can be targeted by reports.
Create an admin to review and audit report submissions (if system logs such events).

scenarios.draft: Test updating fields of a post report as a moderator or admin using PUT /discussionboard/postReports/{id}. Cover success updating resolution status, adding or changing moderator comments, and marking a report as resolved. Attempt to update with invalid fields, update a report that has already been resolved, or update as an unauthorized user (member or unauthenticated), confirming RBAC and business rule enforcement. Verify that audit trail/log is updated for report modification. Should also validate updates fail for deleted/nonexistent report IDs.

dependencies.purpose: Create reporter member for post report creation.
Create a post to serve as a report target.
Create a post report to yield a testable report ID for updating.
Create admin/moderator account required for updating post reports.

scenarios.draft: Test permanent deletion of a post report by admin via DELETE /discussionboard/postReports/{id}. Steps: 1) Successfully delete a report as admin; 2) Attempt to delete the same report twice and confirm correct idempotent or not-found response; 3) Try to delete a report as a non-admin and ensure permission error/forbidden response occurs; 4) Attempt deletion for a non-existent report ID and validate not found or error. Ensure deletion removes the report from all relevant listing endpoints and triggers audit logging for future traceability.

dependencies.purpose: Register a member to file a report.
Create a post to be reported.
Create a post report record to supply a valid report ID for deletion test.
Provision admin account for deleting reports and verifying permission logic.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieving a paginated list of discussion boards with different filter and search conditions, including board name, active/inactive status, category, and date ranges. Verify that only boards visible to the user's role (admin, member) are returned according to permissions. Confirm that pagination works correctly (page/size), and the correct number of records is returned according to applied filters. Include scenarios for empty result set (no matches), invalid filter values (e.g., non-existent category), and permission-restricted data visibility. Also verify sorting functionality (by creation date, activity) as per business logic.

dependencies.purpose: Create several boards with distinct names, active/inactive states, and categories to provide realistic data for advanced filtering and pagination tests.
Create an admin account to perform list/search actions permitted only for admin users.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieving details for a specific discussion board by its UUID. Include a success scenario where the board exists and is active, and users can view public board information. Test failure cases: invalid UUID format, non-existent board (should return 404), and access-denied scenarios (e.g., attempting to access an inactive/soft-deleted board as a non-admin). Additionally, test soft-deleted boards to verify that only admin roles can access as per policy.

dependencies.purpose: Create new board(s) to obtain valid board UUIDs for detail view testing, including both active and inactive boards.

scenarios.draft: Test creating a new discussion board as an admin with valid board data (unique name, required fields), expecting successful creation and correct response data. Also test creation failure when attempting to use a duplicate board name, verifying that the API enforces uniqueness constraint and returns a conflict or validation error. Include a scenario for missing required fields and a scenario where a non-admin actor attempts board creation and is denied.

dependencies.purpose: Create an admin account with permission to create boards.

scenarios.draft: Test updating the metadata of an existing discussion board (name, description, activation state) as an admin. Verify that successful updates reflect in board details and audit logs. Test failure scenarios: update with a duplicate board name (conflict/validation error), update by unauthorized/non-admin actor (permission denied), and updating a non-existent board ID (404 error). Check for correct enforcement of allowed/immutable fields (e.g., cannot change board UUID).

dependencies.purpose: Create a board to obtain a target for update scenarios.
Create an admin account to perform authorized updates.

scenarios.draft: Test soft-deleting (deactivating) a discussion board as an admin. Ensure successful deletion changes board state (inactive/soft-deleted) and the response reflects the correct metadata. Test deletion failure when performed by a non-admin (permission denied) and when attempting to delete a non-existent board ID (404 error). Also, verify business logic that prevents deleting a board with unresolved dependencies (e.g., active threads/posts), ensuring policy errors are returned as required. Validate that deletion is logged for compliance.

dependencies.purpose: Create a board to provide a target for deletion scenarios.
Create an admin account with required permissions.
Create a thread associated with the board to test dependent resource deletion restrictions.

scenarios.draft: Test listing discussion board admins using various filters (e.g. by email, username, and activity state), and test correct pagination. Ensure only users with admin role can access the list. Steps include: (1) Create several admin accounts with unique emails and usernames. (2) Use the PATCH /discussionboard/admins endpoint with different filtering criteria and validate only matching records are returned. (3) Check pagination parameters return the correct subset of records. (4) Attempt the API as a non-admin and verify access is denied.

dependencies.purpose: Create multiple admin accounts to populate data for search/filter tests.

scenarios.draft: Test fetching a discussion board admin by ID. Includes: (1) Creating an admin and then retrieving it by its UUID, validating all details except sensitive fields (e.g. password_hash is not present, but email, username are correct). (2) Attempting to fetch with an invalid UUID format returns validation error. (3) Attempting to fetch a non-existing ID receives a 404 error. (4) Attempting to fetch as a non-admin ensures proper 403 forbidden result.

dependencies.purpose: Create a new admin account to obtain a valid ID for retrieval.

scenarios.draft: Test creating a new admin. Scenario 1: Admin (already authenticated) submits valid unique email, username, and strong password—should succeed, returning new admin record (without password hash) and writing log. Scenario 2: Attempt creation with duplicate email or username—should fail with conflict error. Scenario 3: Attempt with weak password or invalid email—should fail with validation error. Scenario 4: Attempt as non-admin user—should receive forbidden or 401 error.

Test updating a discussion board admin's properties. (1) Valid update by a privileged admin: change email, username, and/or password (uses strong password, validates uniqueness, audit log entry). (2) Attempt as another (non-privileged) admin, or as self without re-authentication (if policy requires), verifying 403 forbidden or fails. (3) Attempt with duplicate email/username triggers validation error. (4) Test that updated details are reflected in a subsequent GET call.

dependencies.purpose: Create admin accounts that can be updated and checked for validation conflicts.

scenarios.draft: Test deleting an admin account by UUID. Scenario 1: Privileged admin deletes a target admin (not themselves); record is soft-deleted (deleted_at set) and can be confirmed by GET showing updated status. Scenario 2: Attempt to delete own account or a non-existent/invalid ID results in forbidden/404. Scenario 3: Ensure audit log is written for the operation. Scenario 4: Attempt to delete as non-admin (401/403 expected).

dependencies.purpose: Create admin accounts to be deleted/verified for audit in the test.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieving a paginated and filtered list of thread follow records. As a regular member, verify that only the threads you follow are listed. As a moderator or admin, confirm access to all follow entries. Include scenarios with and without advanced filtering (such as by member ID, thread ID, follow date). Ensure that results conform to permission boundaries, do not expose unauthorized data, and that pagination and search parameters produce correct result sets. Test invalid parameter values (e.g., non-UUID, negative pagination) and verify error responses for permission violations.

dependencies.purpose: Create member accounts to simulate users following threads with different permissions.
Create threads that can be followed by members.
Create thread follow records to be available for list/search scenarios.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieving a single thread follow record by its ID. As the member who owns the follow, verify that you can successfully retrieve your follow and see all expected fields. As an admin or moderator, verify that any follow can be accessed. Confirm that permission enforcement hides entries from unauthorized users. Test attempting to fetch a follow record as a different, unauthorized member and verify correct error response (e.g., 403/404). Also check the error for non-existent or invalid IDs.

dependencies.purpose: Create at least two member accounts (one owner, one non-owner) to test permission boundaries.
Create a thread that one of the members can follow.
Create a thread follow record, and extract its ID for GET scenario.

scenarios.draft: Test creating a new thread follow as a registered member. First, ensure the member is authenticated and the thread exists. Attempt to follow the same thread twice with the same member and verify that the second attempt fails with a duplicate constraint error (409). Also test creation on non-existent or deleted threads, and as unregistered or unauthorized users, verifying appropriate error responses (403/404).

dependencies.purpose: Create a registered member to act as the authenticated user performing the follow.
Create a legitimate thread for the member to follow.

scenarios.draft: Test updating a thread follow record's mutable fields as the record-owning member (e.g., notification preferences or mute flag), and verify the update is reflected correctly. Attempt the same update as a different member without appropriate permissions and confirm that the operation fails with a forbidden/access error. Attempt to update a follow record that does not exist and verify the correct error response (404).

dependencies.purpose: Register members to serve as the owner and non-owner actors in update scenarios.
Create a thread to generate a thread follow record.
Create the thread follow record and extract its ID for update attempts.

scenarios.draft: Test deleting a thread follow record as the owning member and verify the record is removed (soft or hard deleted per policy), and that unfollow operations update relevant notifications/statistics. Attempt to delete the same record again to ensure idempotence or correct error handling for already-deleted/nonexistent records. Attempt to delete another user's follow record and verify that permission errors are returned (403). Also test as an admin/moderator if permitted by policy.

dependencies.purpose: Register at least two user accounts: owner and non-owner.
Set up thread(s) to follow.
Produce the thread follow record to be deleted and to test permissions.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieving a paginated list of comment edit histories using various filters such as comment ID, editor member ID, and date range. Set up several comments, edit them as different members to create edit history records, then apply filters to verify that only the relevant histories are returned. Ensure pagination returns correct results when there are many histories and check permission enforcement (e.g., only authors or staff can view histories for certain comments). Handle edge cases such as requesting non-existent pages or using invalid filters, and verify error responses for validation failures.

dependencies.purpose: Create initial comments to enable creation of edit histories for those comments.
Edit comments as various members to generate comment edit history records.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieving a single comment edit history record by its ID. First, create a comment, edit it to generate an edit history, then fetch the history by its ID and verify all fields are accurate and permission rules apply. Also attempt to fetch a non-existent or unauthorized record to ensure proper error handling (404 or 403).

dependencies.purpose: Create a comment to allow creation of an edit history.
Edit the comment to generate a comment edit history record.
List comment edit histories to obtain the ID of the created history for retrieval.

scenarios.draft: Test creating a new comment edit history record when a comment is edited. Create a comment, perform an edit with valid data, then explicitly create an edit history entry referencing the comment and editor, providing all required fields. Verify that the new history reflects the edit accurately and that the edit is properly recorded for audit. Attempt to create a history for a comment or editor that does not exist and verify suitable error handling (400/404).

dependencies.purpose: Create a base comment to edit and generate history.
Edit the comment to simulate a real edit before creating an explicit edit history record.

scenarios.draft: Test updating an existing comment edit history entry. After creating a comment and editing it to produce a history, attempt to update metadata such as timestamp or editor with valid data. Verify changes are saved and retrievable. Also attempt to change immutable fields or use invalid data, ensuring the API returns validation errors or denies forbidden changes.

dependencies.purpose: Create a comment to establish a subject for edit history.
Edit the comment to create an edit history entry.
Create an edit history record for update.

scenarios.draft: Test deleting a comment edit history record. After creating a comment and editing it to produce one or more edit histories, delete a history as an authorized user (admin) and confirm it is marked deleted (or redacted per policy). Attempt deletion as an unauthorized user and verify access is denied. Also, test deleting a non-existent or already deleted record and confirm the API returns the correct error status or idempotent handling.

dependencies.purpose: Create a comment and edit it to generate an edit history record for deletion.
Produce an edit event for history generation.
Create a comment edit history record to be deleted.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieving a paginated and filtered list of audit logs using various search and filter criteria, including actor_id, action_type, action_scope, target_id, and date range. Cover scenarios where the requester is an admin and receives matching records, as well as edge cases where filters return zero results. Verify error responses for invalid filters and insufficient permission (non-admin access). Test pagination logic by using different page/size settings. Validate that only admins can access this endpoint, and that audit logs are properly ordered by requested sorting options.

Test fetching a single audit log entry by its UUID. First, as an admin, retrieve an existing audit log and verify that all fields are present and accurate. Test edge cases for non-existent or malformed UUIDs (should return 404 not found or validation error). Confirm that non-admin access is rejected with proper error response. Validate business rule that audit log entries reference only permissible fields without exposing sensitive member data (no passwords, etc.).

dependencies.purpose: Find or create a valid audit log ID to fetch for the valid scenario.

scenarios.draft: Test manual creation of an audit log entry by an admin. Supply required fields including action_type, action_scope, and optionally actor_id/target_id and metadata. Validate successful creation returns all expected log attributes. Test error scenarios for missing required fields (should return 400), invalid actor_id/target_id formats, and permission errors (non-admins). Attempt duplicate creation by ID and verify rejection. Ensure the entry appears in audits listing afterward.

Test updating the metadata, actor_id, or target_id fields on an existing audit log entry. Confirm that only admin users can perform this update and all changes are correctly saved. Attempt to tamper with immutable fields like action_type, action_scope, or creation timestamps, which should return 403/400 errors. Cover scenarios for updating with invalid IDs (404) and unauthorized users. Ensure updates are reflected in subsequent GET requests. Changes made through this endpoint should be themselves logged for meta-audit if required by compliance.

dependencies.purpose: Create a fresh audit log entry for update testing, ensuring known and safe preconditions for updates.

scenarios.draft: Test the soft-deletion (expungement) of a single audit log entry by its UUID, as an admin with special rights. Validate successful deletion returns 204 No Content and verify the action is idempotent (deleting an already-deleted entry has no additional effect beyond compliance logging). Ensure regular admins or unauthorized users cannot delete logs. Test edge cases for not-found and already-deleted entries. Verify that the deleted entry is excluded from subsequent audit log queries unless required by business rules for compliance retention.

dependencies.purpose: Create an audit log entry to ensure there is a testable target for soft-deletion.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieving a paginated, filtered list of community guidelines as various user roles. Validate correct handling of filters (title, version, effective/expired_at, text search), pagination (page index, size), and visibility by user type (regular members, moderators, admins): only current guidelines for members, drafts/history for staff. Include error cases for invalid filters or permissions. Expect results count, summary, and correct ordering.

Verify fetching a single community guideline by UUID. First, create a guideline as an admin or moderator. Confirm that admins and moderators can retrieve any guideline, while members can only access currently effective guidelines. Include tests for requesting non-existent or unauthorized records, expecting 404 or permission denial errors where appropriate.

dependencies.purpose: Create a new community guideline to ensure a valid ID is used for testing single-record retrieval, and to test various access and visibility rules.

scenarios.draft: Test the creation of a new community guideline entry by an admin or moderator. Provide valid data and verify creation success. Attempt creation with invalid data: missing title, duplicate version, overlapping effective periods, or invalid effective/expired_at values. Attempt to create as a non-privileged user and expect permission denied. Confirm each business rule and validation constraint is enforced and only allowed roles can succeed.

Test updating an existing community guideline's details (title, body, version, effective/expired_at) as an admin or moderator. Ensure updates respect business rules: no conflicting versions or periods, no violation of single-current-guideline constraint. Update a record with valid data and verify changes are reflected. Try updating with invalid data (duplicate version, invalid dates) or as unauthorized user, expecting errors and permission denial. Attempt to update a non-existent guideline and check for proper error handling.

dependencies.purpose: Create a guideline to obtain a target ID for update operations and to ensure business rule validations are tested in an existing record context.

scenarios.draft: Test deleting an existing community guideline as an admin or moderator. Ensure deletion respects policy (soft/hard as configured). Confirm that only authorized roles can delete, and deletion is logged. Attempt deletion as unauthorized user and of non-existent or already-deleted records, expecting correct errors and compliance logging. After deletion, verify the guideline is not accessible to role-restricted queries, but still retrievable by audit (if soft-delete/policy applies).

dependencies.purpose: Create a guideline to obtain a valid record for deletion scenarios, ensuring comprehensive business and authorization policy checks during the delete operation.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieval of paginated post edit histories with advanced filtering and sorting. Start by creating a member and two posts. The posts must then be edited to generate edit history records. Verify listing all edit histories for a specific post returns only relevant events. Check that searching by editor or date range restricts results as expected. Also test system limits on page size, and that excessive or malformed filter parameters produce validation errors. Ensure that permission restrictions are enforced so unauthorized members cannot list unrelated edit histories.

dependencies.purpose: Register a member who will author and edit posts, ensuring necessary permissions for edit history creation and filtering.
Create at least two posts by the registered member to generate edit history records for listing and filtering.
Edit the created post(s) to trigger creation of post edit histories by the author.

scenarios.draft: Validate retrieving a specific post edit history entry by its ID. Create a member, a post, and edit the post to generate an edit history. Fetch the edit history by its returned ID and confirm that all expected properties match the edit action. Also attempt to fetch a non-existent or unauthorized edit history (e.g., foreign or deleted ID) and verify error responses for not found or insufficient permissions.

dependencies.purpose: Register a member who will author/edit a post and generate an edit history record.
Create a post by the new member to allow for an edit event.
Edit the post so that a post edit history record is created to retrieve and verify.

scenarios.draft: Test explicit creation of a post edit history entry. Register a member and create a post. Simulate an edit event (either via post update or direct edit history API call) by providing postId, editorId, previous and new values, and a reason. Confirm that the edit history is stored with an assigned ID, correct timestamps, and the appropriate linkage to both the edited post and member. Also verify failures on invalid references (nonexistent post or editor) and that duplicate/history overwrite rules are correctly enforced by policy.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member to use as the post author and the editor for edit events.
Create a post which will be edited and for which the edit history will refer.

scenarios.draft: Verify that only admins can modify a post edit history record, such as for correcting metadata or updating audit reason. Begin by registering an admin and a regular member, then have the member create and edit a post. Capture the edit history. As an admin, update certain allowed metadata fields of the edit history record. Confirm that changes are reflected and audit logs are updated. Attempt to update restricted fields or as a non-admin, and ensure errors are returned for unauthorized changes or invalid input.

dependencies.purpose: Register a member to create and edit a post (generating the edit history).
Register an admin account for permission testing and update attempts.
Create a post that will be edited (edit history required for update test).
Edit the post as the member to generate at least one edit history record for subsequent update by admin.

scenarios.draft: Test admin compliance deletion of a post edit history record. Register both a member (to create a post and edit it) and an admin. The member edits their post to create an edit history. The admin then deletes the edit history (for compliance or correction). Confirm that deleted records cannot be retrieved afterward, and that all deletions are properly audited. Attempt deletion attempts as a non-admin and ensure they fail with correct permission errors. Retry deleting an already deleted or non-existent history entry to verify appropriate error handling and idempotency.

dependencies.purpose: Register a member to author, edit, and create the edit history record.
Admin registration to test privileged-only deletion.
Create a post to edit and thus construct an edit history entry.
Edit the post to create the history entry to be deleted.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieving a paginated, filtered list of comments from the discussion board. Verify that filters (such as by post ID, author ID, parent ID, and date range) correctly limit results. Confirm that pagination works properly, returning expected results for different page/size parameters. Validate that members can only access comments in accordance with their role/permissions (e.g., soft-deleted or flagged content is only visible to moderators or admins). Test invalid query parameters and confirm that proper error responses are returned for validation failures. Also test performance with large result sets to ensure pagination remains efficient.

dependencies.purpose: Create a post as a prerequisite for associating comments and enabling filter tests.
Register members who will author comments and perform retrieval operations.
Create comments with diverse properties (including replies/parent-child relationships, and various timestamps) to populate the database for list/filter scenarios.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieving the full detail of a specific comment by ID. Ensure that access control rules are strictly enforced: ordinary members can see public comments, but soft-deleted/flagged comments are only returned for moderators or admins. Attempt to retrieve non-existent comment IDs and verify that an appropriate error (not found) is returned. Validate rejection and error messages for malformed/non-UUID IDs. Confirm that audit fields and parent/post linkage are properly included in the response.

dependencies.purpose: Create a comment for retrieval and permission tests. This sets up valid IDs and allows for manipulation of comment visibility/status.
Register members with different roles (member, moderator, admin) for testing permission scenarios.

scenarios.draft: Test creating a new comment under different scenarios: (a) as a simple comment reply to a post, (b) as a nested reply to an existing comment, (c) providing all required fields, and (d) omitting required fields or using invalid post/comment IDs. Validate that only authenticated members can create comments and attempts by unauthenticated actors are rejected. Test spam/abuse logic by submitting duplicate or rapid comments to the same post. Attempt to reference deleted or invalid parent/post and check for the appropriate error response (not found/validation error).

dependencies.purpose: Create a post to which the new comment will be attached.
Create an initial comment to test nested replies/parent-child relationships.
Register members to act as comment authors in role-based validation checks.

scenarios.draft: Test that unauthenticated users (i.e., not logged in) are unable to create comments. Attempt to submit a new comment without authentication and validate that the response is an error indicating permissions failure.

dependencies.purpose: Create a post to which the attempted unauthenticated comment will be targeted.

scenarios.draft: Test editing a comment by its ID in various scenarios: (a) as the comment's author during the allowed edit window, (b) as a moderator/admin for compliance, and (c) by unauthorized users (not the author or lacking correct permission). Confirm that edits to body, deleted status, and review status are properly validated and logged in edit history. Attempt updates after the edit window has expired, or for comments that do not exist, and confirm handling of error scenarios and audit trail creation.

dependencies.purpose: Create a comment that can be updated, providing a known comment ID for update and permission scenarios.
Register members (the comment's author, a moderator, and another unrelated user) to test various permission cases.

scenarios.draft: Test deleting a comment with various permission scenarios and deletion policies: (a) soft-deletion by the comment author or moderator/admin; (b) hard/permanent deletion by authorized admin; (c) attempt by unauthorized user (not author or lacking permissions); (d) deletion of already deleted or non-existent comments. Confirm audit logging, notification triggers, and any moderation workflows. Validate the state of the comment record after deletion (soft-deleted status, metadata updates, etc.) and check that subsequent fetch/list calls reflect correct deletion state and permissions.

dependencies.purpose: Create comments to be deleted, including parent and child cases for cascade/edge-case handling.
Register different user roles to test deletion permissions and audit tracking.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieving a paginated list of comment dislikes with various filters such as comment ID, member ID, and date ranges. Ensure that the list only includes dislikes the user is permitted to view based on their role: members can see their own dislikes and moderators/admins can see any. Verify that pagination and sorting work as expected, that malformed queries return validation errors, and insufficient permission attempts are correctly rejected. Setup at least two members, a moderator, and several comments with dislikes to simulate real scenarios.

dependencies.purpose: Create multiple members (including a moderator) to test permission scopes for listing dislikes.
Create several comments for testing filtered dislike retrieval.
Create comment dislike records by different members to enable meaningful search/filter/pagination tests.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieving the detail of a single comment dislike event by its ID. Confirm that only the member who created the dislike, or a moderator/admin, can access the record; others are denied. Attempt to access a non-existent ID and a dislike that does not belong to the current user (when not admin/moderator) to ensure proper error responses. Validate that all returned fields match the schema. Scenario includes both a valid and invalid ID check.

dependencies.purpose: Create members and a moderator/admin to check different access patterns.
Create a comment for use in the dislike operation.
Generate a dislike on the created comment for fetching by ID.

scenarios.draft: Test successful creation of a comment dislike by an authenticated member. Ensure that the operation fails with a business error when a duplicate dislike is attempted (same member disliking same comment twice). Also ensure that a dislike cannot be created against a non-existent or deleted comment, and that non-authenticated users are denied access. Scenario must create member, comment, and verify error handling across all conditions.

dependencies.purpose: Register a member who will perform the dislike operation.
Create a comment for the member to dislike.

scenarios.draft: Test updating metadata fields (such as audit info) on a comment dislike record by an admin or moderator. Confirm that regular members cannot update dislike records. Attempt updating a non-existent record to verify error handling. Validate that immutable fields (like comment/member association) cannot be changed, and all changes are audit-logged.

dependencies.purpose: Create a moderator/admin to perform update.
Create a comment for which a dislike will be created.
Create a comment dislike to update.

scenarios.draft: Test deletion (undislike) of a comment dislike record by the owner (member) and by moderators/admins. Ensure that deleting a non-existent dislike is handled idempotently and does not result in an error. Confirm only the owner or staff can delete; unauthorized deletion attempts by other members should fail with correct errors. Ensure the deleted record is removed appropriately and cascades work if the member or comment is deleted.

dependencies.purpose: Create members and a moderator/admin for delete operation scenarios.
Create a comment to generate dislikes for deletion.
Create the comment dislike records to be deleted.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieving a paginated and filtered list of policy update events. Begin by creating multiple policy update events through the create endpoint to ensure variety in actors, policies, and timestamps. Use specific filters such as actor, policy_id, and date range to search for updates, and verify the correct subset is returned for different filter criteria. Test pagination by limiting the page size and checking that multiple pages return the full dataset. Validate behavior when filters return zero results and when invalid filters are supplied. Confirm access restrictions—only admins and moderators may access this list. Ensure that unauthorized users are denied access with a proper error response and that malformed queries return validation errors.

dependencies.purpose: Create multiple policy update events to ensure the presence of diverse data for listing and filtering scenarios.
Create policy documents to be referenced by policy update logs, establishing data context.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieving a single policy update event by its ID. First, create a policy and an associated update event. Fetch the event by its UUID and verify all properties (policy, actor, summary, timestamp) match the expected data. Attempt retrieval with a non-existent or deleted ID to ensure a 'not found' error is returned. Test access control by attempting to retrieve an event as an unauthorized user and confirm that proper permission errors are given. Verify that audit log integrity is preserved for all accesses.

dependencies.purpose: Create a policy update event to obtain a valid ID for detail retrieval.
Create a policy as a prerequisite to referencing it in the policy update event.

scenarios.draft: Test creating a new policy update event. Start by creating an admin and a policy record to reference. Attempt to create the policy update event using valid and required information, verifying the event is created with correct actor, policy, summary, and timestamp. Attempt to create an event with missing required fields (e.g., no policy reference, missing actor, or summary) and with invalid references (nonexistent policy or actor) to verify that validation and referential integrity errors are returned. Attempt creation as a non-admin user to confirm that authorization is enforced. Confirm that all successful creates are logged and retrievable in subsequent listing operations.

dependencies.purpose: Create a policy document to reference when recording a policy update log.
List or create an admin user to act as the authority recording the policy update event.

scenarios.draft: Test updating an existing policy update event. First, create a policy and a policy update event as prerequisites to ensure an editable record exists. Attempt to update the summary, actor, or referenced policy as an authorized admin, verifying updates are reflected in the response and follow audit trail requirements. Attempt to change to an invalid referenced policy or set fields to invalid values to ensure validation errors appear. Attempt to update as a non-admin and confirm access is denied. Attempt to update a non-existent or already-deleted event and verify that a 'not found' error is returned. Ensure no fields outside the allowed set can be modified, and policy audit logging remains consistent after changes.

dependencies.purpose: Create a policy update event to allow for editing/updating.
Create a policy to be referenced or changed in update operation.

scenarios.draft: Test deleting a single policy update event. First, create a policy and an associated update event to be deleted. Attempt deletion as an authorized admin and verify confirmation or soft-delete status; ensure the event is no longer retrievable via get/list endpoints. Attempt to delete with a non-existent or already-deleted ID and check for proper error response. Attempt as a non-admin and verify permission error. Confirm that the deletion is logged in the system audit trail for compliance and that downstream references are unaffected or gracefully handled.

dependencies.purpose: Create a policy update event for deletion testing.
Create a policy referenced by the policy update event.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieving a paginated, filtered list of search history records for a member by applying a keyword filter and a specified timeframe. 1) Create a member and generate multiple search history entries with various keywords and timestamps. 2) Attempt to retrieve the search history with filters matching only a subset of those entries (by keyword and timeframe), and verify the correct records are returned. 3) Check that the pagination metadata reflects the matching subset only. Failure scenario: Provide an invalid date format or attempt retrieval for another member as a non-admin, expecting a permission error or validation error.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member account to associate with the search histories for context and permissions.
Create multiple search history records for the member, varying in keywords and timestamps to enable filter testing.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieving a single search history entry by its ID in two cases: (1) As the member who owns the search history (expecting full details) and (2) As an admin (expecting broader access). Set up includes creating a member, logging a search history entry, and attempting to retrieve it with appropriate permissions. Also test failure: provide a non-existent or unauthorized ID (as a different user/member) and expect a 404 or permission error.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member account to associate with search history.
Create a search history entry to retrieve.
Create an admin user for the admin scenario and to test broader retrieval permissions.

scenarios.draft: Test creating a search history record for a member after authenticating. 1) Register a new member. 2) Authenticate as the member and submit a search query via POST. 3) Verify the created record contains the expected search keywords, filters, and timestamps. Failure: Attempt to create a search history record as an unauthenticated user or for a different member's account, expecting a permission or validation error.

dependencies.purpose: Create a new member to simulate member authentication.

scenarios.draft: Test updating fields of an existing search history entry as the record owner. Set up includes creating a member and a corresponding search history entry. The member then updates the record's search keywords/filters. Verify that the update is persisted and visible on subsequent fetch. Negative case: Another member or unauthenticated user attempts the update, which should fail with a permission error.

dependencies.purpose: Create the owner member.
Create a search history record to update.
Create a secondary member for negative permission scenario.

scenarios.draft: Test deletion of a search history record by the member who created it. (1) Successfully delete as the owner and confirm the record is no longer retrievable. (2) Attempt to delete the record as another member or unauthenticated user—expect a forbidden or not found error. Also test deletion of a record that does not exist or has already been deleted, expecting safe idempotency or a clear error.

dependencies.purpose: Create the owner member.
Create the search history record to be deleted.
Create a secondary member for negative permission scenario.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieving a paginated and searchable list of discussion board policies, validating support for various filter criteria such as effective date, title, version, and ordering. Simulate requests for different roles: admin, moderator, and general member, verifying that non-public or expired policies are restricted to authorized viewers only. Check for correct pagination metadata and that results contain only the allowed policies for the role and filters used. Attempt invalid or malformed filters to verify that meaningful validation errors are returned and that access is denied for unauthorized roles. Also test combinations that yield empty result sets (e.g., searching for a non-existent title) to check that system responds gracefully.

Test retrieving the details of a specific policy via its unique ID. Scenarios must include: 1) An admin or moderator retrieving any policy (including expired/draft) and receiving full details; 2) A member retrieving only currently effective policies, verifying that access is denied for non-public or expired ones; 3) Attempt to fetch a non-existent policy ID to confirm correct 404 handling; 4) Role-based validation ensuring sensitive, retired, or draft policies are not accessible to unauthorized users; 5) All relevant errors and access controls are robustly enforced.

dependencies.purpose: Create policy records to ensure specific IDs exist for retrieval and access control tests.

scenarios.draft: Test creating a new policy record as an admin user with valid details, verifying that all required metadata (title, content, version, effective and expiry dates) must be present and correct, and that success returns the newly created policy's detail. Also include scenarios for failure: attempt creation with missing or duplicate (title/version), invalid dates (invalid format, expiry before effective), or by a non-admin user, confirming permission errors and validation error responses. All successful creations should be logged in audit trail per business requirements.

Test updating a policy document by its ID as an admin. Success case: change title, content, or date fields and confirm the record is updated and the change is recorded for audit. Failure cases: attempt by a non-admin actor, attempt updates on non-existent or expired/deleted records (returning errors), try to update with a duplicate version or conflicting dates (ensure validation blocks), and check that all changes are logged and versioned for compliance reporting. Ensure only currently allowed fields can be updated and others are ignored or rejected.

dependencies.purpose: Create a baseline policy to update and test various update scenarios (including version conflict and field changes).

scenarios.draft: Test deletion (expiration/retirement) of a policy as a system admin. Success: mark a live policy as expired/deleted and ensure it's retained for transparency and not shown as active. Failure: attempt deletion on a non-existent or already-retired policy (expect an error), unauthorized (non-admin) deletion to verify permission is enforced, and confirm all deletions are properly logged. Confirm that deleted policies cannot be used in subsequent business operations and remain accessible for compliance/audit as appropriate.

dependencies.purpose: Create a new policy for deletion tests and to establish test fixtures for expired or retired state validation.

scenarios.draft: Test successful retrieval of a paginated, filtered moderator assignment list for an admin actor. Cover scenarios filtering by assigned member, grantor, status (active, revoked), and grant time range. Confirm the API supports varied combinations and returns metadata for pagination. Verify robust handling of filters returning no results. Include both large and small result sets to check performance and response consistency. Include validation for RBAC outcomes—ensure forbidden for non-admins. Test for failure on malformed query or excessive pagination requests.

dependencies.purpose: Create admin user(s) to act as grantor and to perform moderator assignment/retrieval actions.
Create regular members on whom moderator assignments will be granted.
Create several moderator assignments to populate the listing, with varying statuses and grantors.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieving a specific moderator assignment by ID with sufficient privileges. Ensure all fields are accurately returned, including relevant member/admin IDs, grant metadata, and timestamps. Confirm that the data matches latest assignment state. Check that only admins can access and that 404 is returned when the ID does not exist. Also, verify that forbidden errors are triggered for invalid/non-admin access attempts.

dependencies.purpose: Create an admin who will retrieve the moderator assignment.
Create a target member for moderator assignment.
Establish a moderator assignment to retrieve by ID.

scenarios.draft: Test creating a moderator assignment for a member using valid data and sufficient admin privileges. Ensure a corresponding assignment is created and correct data is reflected, including grantor, assigned member, and timestamp. Test rejection if the member is already an active moderator or if invalid member/grantor IDs are provided. Attempt creation without sufficient privileges (non-admin actor) and validate that the system returns a permission error. Verify that attempts to assign to non-existent or deleted members result in errors. Confirm correct audit log event is triggered on success.

dependencies.purpose: Create an admin who can grant moderator.
Create a member to be assigned as moderator.

scenarios.draft: Test updating moderator assignment metadata by ID using an admin user. Cover common cases: updating revoke timestamp, changing grantor or related notes. Test for 404 error if ID does not exist and ensure permission is checked—only admins can perform update. Validate that fields not allowed for update (e.g., non-metadata) are rejected or ignored. Ensure system logs the change and state transitions accurately, and confirm correct updated data is returned.

dependencies.purpose: Create an admin to execute update operations.
Create a member for initial moderator assignment.
Create a moderator assignment to update.

scenarios.draft: Test deletion of a moderator assignment by ID using admin privileges. Confirm hard/soft deletion as per business policy and ensure assignment is no longer returned in listings or detail endpoints. Test deletion of already-deleted or non-existent assignments (should be idempotent or return 404). Confirm that only admins can perform deletions—attempts by non-admins should fail with permission errors. Ensure audit log entry is created for the delete action and related notifications are triggered if applicable.

dependencies.purpose: Create an admin with privilege to delete moderator assignments.
Provision members to create moderator assignments.
Create a moderator assignment to be deleted.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieving a paginated, filtered list of notifications for a member. Set up a member with a variety of notifications for different types and channels (e.g., on_site, email), both read and unread, and across a range of dates. Validate that the API returns the expected notifications based on provided filtering criteria, pagination parameters (page/size), type filters, and read status. Confirm that only notifications belonging to the authenticated member (or, if admin, any member) are returned, and the pagination metadata accurately reflects the total number of entries. Also test edge cases where no notifications match the filter, and verify permission errors when accessing notifications as an unauthorized user.

dependencies.purpose: Create several notifications for a target member to establish test data for listing and filtering.
Register a member who will own the notifications.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieving a single notification by its ID. Start by creating a notification for a particular member, then attempt to fetch it as: 1) the owner of the notification (should succeed), 2) another member (should be forbidden), 3) an admin (should succeed for audit cases), and 4) with an invalid or non-existent ID (should return a not found error). Validate that access control rules are enforced strictly so that members only see their own notifications, while admins can see any. Also, verify the complete details in the notification response match the originally created notification data.

dependencies.purpose: Create a notification to obtain a valid notification ID for retrieval tests.
Register members (both the owner and non-owner) for testing access scenarios.
Register an admin user to test admin access to notifications.

scenarios.draft: Test the creation of notification records with valid and invalid payloads. Valid case: as an admin, create a notification with all required fields (target member, type, entity references, channel, message, timestamps). Invalid cases: attempt to create a notification for a non-existent member, or with missing required fields (e.g., missing notification type or target member). Also, test attempting to create notifications as a non-admin or unauthenticated user (should be forbidden). Validate behavior for each of these paths and confirm audit logging is triggered on success.

dependencies.purpose: Register a valid member to receive the notification.
Register and authenticate an admin to perform notification creation.

scenarios.draft: Test updating a notification's read/unread status and possibly correcting message metadata. As the owner member, mark a notification as read and verify the updated state is reflected in the response and subsequent get/list queries. As an admin, update fields as allowed for compliance/audit (e.g., correcting a delivery channel or message). Test forbidden updates by unauthorized users. Test updating an already-deleted or non-existent notification (should return not found or appropriate error).

dependencies.purpose: Create a notification to provide a target for update testing.
Register a member who will update their own notification.
Register an admin to test privileged updates.

scenarios.draft: Test deletion of a notification record both by the owning member and by an admin. Create a notification for a member; have the member delete it and confirm it is no longer returned by list/detail endpoints. Have an admin delete a notification belonging to any member and confirm deletion is effective. Attempt deletion of a non-existent or already-deleted notification, and see that appropriate errors are returned. Attempt unauthorized deletion (another member or unauthenticated user) and verify permission denial. Confirm deletion triggers audit logging and that any deletion side-effects (such as notification count for the member) are reflected properly.

dependencies.purpose: Create a notification to test deletion scenarios.
Register a member who will delete their own notification.
Register an admin to test authorized deletion by staff.

scenarios.draft: Test listing and searching board tag entities with different filters and pagination settings as an admin user. This scenario includes filtering by tag name, associated board, and creation date, as well as sorting by different criteria and requesting different pages/sizes for results. The scenario should verify that the correct entities are returned for each set of parameters, and should also test that unauthorized users are either denied or limited to permitted results. Error responses must be validated for invalid query filters or malformed pagination parameters.

dependencies.purpose: Create multiple board tag entities with varied tag values and associated boards to test search, filtering, and pagination.
Create boards for board tag association and to provide data for filtering by board.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieval of detailed board tag information using a valid tag ID and with an invalid or non-existent ID. The scenario covers the happy path where a valid board tag ID returns complete detail, and error cases where the ID does not exist or the user lacks permission. Also include permission boundary tests for non-admin users if any restrictions apply.

dependencies.purpose: Create a board tag entity to obtain a valid ID for detail lookup.

scenarios.draft: Test creation of a board tag entity with valid input as an admin, expecting a successful response with correct details, and then attempt to create another board tag with the same name and board association to validate enforcement of uniqueness constraints. Also test creating with missing required fields or unauthorized user, and ensure appropriate error responses are returned.

dependencies.purpose: Create a board entity to associate with the new board tag.

scenarios.draft: Test the failure case when attempting to create a board tag for a board that does not exist (invalid board ID). The response should be a validation or foreign key constraint error indicating that the provided board ID is invalid or not found.

Test updating a board tag by ID with valid data as an admin, such as changing the tag name or associated board. Validate success and that the returned data matches the update. Next, attempt to update using a duplicate name/board combination to trigger a uniqueness conflict, and with invalid or nonexistent tag ID to trigger not found errors. Test missing required fields and unauthorized access as well.

dependencies.purpose: Create a board tag to serve as the target for update tests.
Create another board tag with unique data to simulate a duplicate scenario for the uniqueness check.
Create a board to test board association update and validation.

scenarios.draft: Test soft-deleting a board tag entity by ID as an admin. After confirming successful deletion and correct status, attempt to delete the same board tag again and verify idempotent result or appropriate already-deleted status. Also test deletion with an invalid or non-existent ID for correct error response. Validate that references to deleted tags are handled appropriately in dependent features (e.g., tag listings or analytics).

dependencies.purpose: Create a board tag to be deleted in this scenario.

scenarios.draft: Test an admin listing channels with various filter and search settings (e.g. filtering by visibility, searching by partial channel name, filtering by creation date range, and using different sorting orders). Ensure pagination works as expected, and only relevant channels are shown according to filter criteria. The draft should include verifying that all fields match the request filters, and response metadata matches query settings.

dependencies.purpose: Create multiple channels with differing names, visibilities, and timestamps to allow testing of filtering, searching, and pagination constraints. This step is required to setup diverse test data for the query scenarios.
Create and login as an admin to ensure full permission for exhaustive channel search.

scenarios.draft: Test that a non-admin member or moderator can only see public or permitted channels when listing channels (hidden or deleted channels should not appear to these roles, even if included via search query). Validate that the returned list excludes forbidden channels and proper error or empty states are shown if no permissible channels exist. Also verify that querying deleted or hidden channels as non-admin does not succeed.

dependencies.purpose: Create both public and hidden channels to test permission-restricted access in the list operation.
Register a normal member user who lacks admin privileges.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieving detailed info for a variety of channel IDs as both admin and normal member. Ensure full details are returned for admins, but members cannot access hidden or soft-deleted channels. For normal, public channels, both admin and member should succeed; for hidden/deleted, only admin should succeed, with members receiving permission errors.

dependencies.purpose: Create a mix of public, hidden, and deleted channels to use as test targets for the channel detail endpoint.
Create and login as an admin to validate admin-specific access.
Create and login as a normal member to test permission boundaries when accessing channel details.

scenarios.draft: Attempt to retrieve details for channel IDs that do not exist or have been deleted. Validate that 404 or appropriate not-found/permission errors are returned, and ensure error messages are informative and security-compliant (no internal info leak).

dependencies.purpose: Soft-delete a channel, then attempt to retrieve its details to verify inaccessibility for non-admin roles.
Create an admin for use in making invalid requests as both admin and member to differentiate error behaviors.

scenarios.draft: Test creation of a new channel by an admin using a unique name, valid description, and different visibility statuses (public, hidden). Should successfully create channel and return all fields as expected, verifying uniqueness and correct visibility setting.

dependencies.purpose: Create an admin user as only admins are allowed to create channels.

scenarios.draft: Test failure when an admin attempts to create a channel with a duplicate name, or is missing required fields in the payload (like name or description). Validate that the API returns detailed validation errors or uniqueness violation messages, and no extra channels are created in the DB.

dependencies.purpose: Create an initial channel to setup a duplicate name scenario for later requests.
Create the admin user required for channel operations.

scenarios.draft: Test attempt to create a channel as a non-admin (normal member or moderator). Validate that the API rejects the operation with a permission error, and no channel is created as a result.

dependencies.purpose: Create and login as a normal member to test permission error on channel creation.

scenarios.draft: Test an admin updating a channel's metadata fields (such as name, description, visibility status) and verify that only mutable fields are changed and reflected in the returned entity. Test updating to new unique names and changing visibility from public to hidden and vice versa.

dependencies.purpose: Create a channel whose metadata and visibility will be updated.
Create an admin account for running the authorized update scenario.

scenarios.draft: Test updating a channel's name to a value that already exists on another channel, or supplying invalid request data (empty name, invalid visibility). The API should enforce uniqueness, validation, and return appropriate errors, ensuring no improper changes applied.

dependencies.purpose: Create two channels to test update conflict for duplicate name scenario.
Create admin to perform the updates as only admin is permitted.

scenarios.draft: Test attempt to update a channel via this endpoint as a non-admin (member or moderator). The API should reject the request with permission error, and the entity should remain unchanged.

dependencies.purpose: Create a channel by admin, to later be targeted for unauthorized update attempt.
Create a normal member for testing permission error on update.

scenarios.draft: Test soft-deleting a channel as an admin: ensure the API marks the channel as deleted (without hard removal), that the soft-deleted channel becomes inaccessible for non-admin users, and appropriate audit information or deletion context is returned. Verify that listing and detail endpoints reflect the new state correctly for all roles.

dependencies.purpose: Create a channel eligible for deletion during the test.
Create and login as admin, since deletion requires admin role.

scenarios.draft: Attempt to soft-delete a channel as a non-admin (e.g. member or moderator). Verify that the operation is rejected due to insufficient privileges, and the channel remains accessible/unchanged. Ensure no side effects and the response contains correct permission denial messages.

dependencies.purpose: Create a test channel, initially by admin, to provide a target for unauthorized deletion test.
Register a normal member who will attempt to perform the forbidden delete action.

scenarios.draft: Try deleting a channel that is already soft-deleted, as an admin. Ensure idempotent compliance: no error beyond any required notification, repeated deletion logs action but does not cause duplicate or erroneous side effects. Should continue to block the channel from member access.

dependencies.purpose: Create a channel, then soft-delete it in setup, to enable attempt to delete already-deleted channel.
Admin required for both initial delete and repeat delete scenario.

scenarios.draft: Test successfully searching and listing board sections using different filters and pagination options. Use an admin account to ensure full access rights. Scenario includes filtering by channel, searching by partial section name, filtering by visibility, and paging through results with non-default parameters (e.g., larger than default page size). Validate that results, counts, and pagination fields are correctly formed and match the expected filtered dataset. Dependencies include authenticated admin session and existing sections for meaningful pagination/filters.

dependencies.purpose: Create several distinct sections in different channels to populate data for pagination and filtering. Should occur after authenticating as admin.
Create at least two channels to associate sections with, covering channel filtering and assignment.

scenarios.draft: Test searching/listing board sections with filter values that do not match any records (e.g., using a random string for section name or selecting a channel UUID with no sections). Use admin credentials to ensure permissions are not blocking the test. Confirm that the response includes an empty result list with correct pagination metadata, and verify no permission or error is produced for empty result sets.
